name: introduction to obesity overview
title: Obesity management by body mass index: lifestyle and psychology for everyone; a drug (tirzepatide or semaglutide first, naltrexone-bupropion next) at BMI 30, or 27 with complications; bariatric surgery at BMI 40, 35 with a complication, or 30 with poorly controlled type 2 diabetes; each column gives what to check before, what to give, and what to expect or watch

root.title: Obesity: how far up the ladder? BMI + complications decide
lines: body mass index (BMI) ≥ 30, or ≥ 25 South or East Asian · always with waist circumference
ASK permission first · ASSESS the 4 M's (mental, mechanical, metabolic, monetary)
rule out hypothyroidism, Cushing's, medications · A1c, lipids, thyroid-stimulating hormone, alanine aminotransferase

groups.title: EVERYONE, whatever the BMI
lines: goal: health and well-being, not a number

groups.title: BMI ≥ 30, or ≥ 27 with complications: ADD A DRUG
lines: ≥ 5% loss by 12 weeks at the maximum tolerated dose, else switch · likely lifelong

groups.title: BMI ≥ 40, ≥ 35 + a complication, or ≥ 30 + poorly controlled type 2 diabetes: SURGERY

head: h
Lifestyle + psychology
the base under every other step
clue: • cardiology referral before exercise, if needed
inv: • healthy eating, ideally with a dietitian
tx: activity: little loss, but keeps it off

head: h
Tirzepatide > semaglutide
glucagon-like peptide 1 (GLP-1) agonists; tirzepatide adds glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)
the most effective drugs
clue: other cautions: see the GLUCOSE-LOWERING DRUGS tree
tx: absorption of other drugs changes, e.g. the pill

head: h
Naltrexone-bupropion
one oral tablet
orlistat: rarely, weak + side effects
clue: • pregnancy, any OPIOID use, monoamine oxidase inhibitor
• uncontrolled hypertension, renal or liver failure
inv: Build up to 2 tablets twice daily

head: h
Bariatric surgery
sleeve or Roux-en-Y bypass most common
gastric band: no longer done
clue: • unstable psychiatric illness, untreated substance use
inv: type 2 diabetes, fatty liver, polycystic ovary syndrome, sleep apnea improve or remit
tx: • iron, B12, calcium + vitamin D, vitamin A
Wernicke's: 1–3 months post-op, nausea, poor intake
